R_lts_inland.name: Inland Harbor Phase
R_lts_inland.description: Adapted inland Harbor Phase: safe, automated, materially stable, socially alive, and genuinely livable. The leads are restless for different personal reasons rather than collectively trapped in a failed society.
R_lts_inland.text: Inland Harbor Phase — Adapted coastal city of occupied apartments, raised transit, flood-control gates, shops, bars, workplaces, playgrounds, public screens and covered walkways. Soft gray-blue rain, civic glass, wet paving, warm interior windows and practical public lighting.

R_lts_threshold.name: Threshold / Floodwall
R_lts_threshold.description: The boundary where tide-running leaves the managed city: old ferry lot, staging area, flood steps, tide boards.
R_lts_threshold.text: Threshold / Floodwall — Old ferry lot, staging area, flood steps and tide boards against the massive floodwall. Wet asphalt, cold mist, open car trunks, vehicle headlights, contractor-white work lights and dark concrete.

R_lts_flats.name: The Flats
R_lts_flats.description: Exposed seabed crossing: mud, old pavement, channels, broken pilings, fog, returning water.
R_lts_flats.text: The Flats — Exposed seabed of black tidal mud, old pavement, channels, broken pilings, shell debris, shallow teal pools and dense fog. Boots sink and splash; distant sodium reflections shimmer across wet surfaces.

R_lts_reach.name: The Reach
R_lts_reach.description: Abandoned offshore districts: fixed physical geography exposed by low tides. Dangerous because real, not because supernatural.
R_lts_reach.text: The Reach — Salt-stained abandoned offshore districts exposed at low tide: wet concrete, rusted railings, flooded lower levels, broken walkways, black water, deep cyan fog and faded institutional-green surfaces. Headlamps and work lights fall off quickly in fog.
